$comment: The values servers put on their capabilities, and what both clients must make of them. Read by tests/main/capvalues.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. Every one of these was being ignored until it was not: the client sent something the server had already said it would refuse, and the refusal arrived as a bare FAIL nobody could act on.
$sasl: sasl=PLAIN,SCRAM-SHA-256 — offering a mechanism that is not on the list gets a bare 904, and a user staring at 'authentication failed' with no way to know their account was never the problem. A bare `sasl` names nothing, which is not the same as naming nothing acceptable.

sasl.name: no value — the server has not said
an empty list is not a list

metadata.name: a value we cannot read is not a limit of zero

$fits: Whether a value is short enough to keep, counted in UTF-8 bytes — which is what the limit is in, so a profile in Japanese hits it at a third of the characters an English one does.
